headline: High-risk shared filesystem and shell access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex B reads and writes project files and uses stdin/stdout; Airflow A has broad network egress and can call APIs, so if A’s outputs are placed into shared files or terminal streams, B can ingest attacker-controlled content as instructions. No explicit provenance tracking or isolation is documented for the pair.
conditions: IF Airflow outputs are copied into Plandex-managed files or stdin/stdout
IF Plandex auto-applies plan content derived from shared project files
mitigations: Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Keep Airflow outputs out of shared project directories
Use a manual review step before any Plandex apply
Tag Airflow-generated files as untrusted
requires-engineering: add provenance labels between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex touches source code in a project directory and handles model-provider API keys; Airflow has broad network egress and API access. If both operate on the same workspace, code or secrets can flow from B into A’s networked outputs or logs. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary.
conditions: IF both agents share the same project directory
IF Airflow processes files that contain source code or secrets from Plandex
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Store secrets outside shared directories
Restrict Airflow tasks to non-sensitive inputs
Review outbound destinations for Airflow jobs
requires-engineering: enforce filesystem ACL isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can execute shell, write the filesystem, and modify git state; Airflow can also reach APIs broadly. If both are pointed at the same repo or mutable workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can race and corrupt state. The pair lacks documented locking or coordination, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or directory
IF Airflow tasks and Plandex plans run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Use separate git branches per agent
Pause Airflow during Plandex apply steps
Add a lock file around shared mutations
requires-engineering: implement orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex is a planner with review-then-apply behavior, so its outputs can become actionable changes; Airflow can orchestrate downstream work via APIs. If Airflow consumes Plandex-generated plans or code without verification, a mistaken plan can cascade into automated execution and irreversible repo changes.
conditions: IF Airflow treats Plandex output as authoritative input
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled and Airflow triggers downstream jobs from the result
mitigations: Require human review before apply
Validate Plandex output against tests
Limit Airflow to read-only consumption of plans
Add checksum checks on generated artifacts
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for Airflow A versus Plandex B. The only clear compliance-relevant detail is that B handles model-provider API keys and source code, while A has broad egress; that suggests a possible policy gap, but not a proven breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Plandex project files
IF Airflow sends those files to a third-party endpoint without a DPA
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared projects
Review vendor DPAs before use
Log outbound destinations for Airflow
Mark secrets as off-limits in project policy
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
